svg.title: A 51-year-old client reports irregular menses over the past year along with hot flashes and diaphoresis that disrupt sleep, plus vaginal dryness with painful intercourse. Labs show an elevated FSH level.
svg.desc: Menopause labs show falling estrogen and progesterone with a rising FSH, and this client's vasomotor findings (hot flashes, diaphoresis disrupting sleep) and genitourinary findings (vaginal dryness, painful intercourse) are classic for perimenopause/menopause. A water-soluble lubricant for dyspareunia and weight-bearing exercise to protect bone and muscle are appropriate recommendations. AUB from fibroids centers on irregular heavy bleeding rather than vasomotor symptoms with a rising FSH, and PMDD symptoms cluster before menses and ease after onset rather than persisting for a full year. Estrogen-only therapy is only safe without a uterus; giving it regardless of uterine status risks endometrial cancer if the uterus is intact.
